description:
Rahara Parent, Baby and Toddler Group meets every Friday during the school term at Rahara National School on the Athleague Road, Co. Roscommon, running from 10am to 12pm. Parents, grandparents and childminders are all welcome to bring along babies through to preschoolers aged 0-5.

It's a relaxed, low-key morning built around a chat over tea and a biscuit while the children play, with a small contribution of €2 per adult covering the session. Those who'd like to stay in the loop can leave their name and mobile number on a Friday to be added to the group's WhatsApp.

Known locally as Little Live Wires, Rooskey Parent, Baby and Toddler Group gathers every Friday from 10.15am to 12.15pm at Rooskey Community Centre on Main Street, Co. Roscommon. There's no need to book - mums, dads, grandparents, childminders and carers from any area are free to just turn up with their babies and kids.

A good selection of toys keeps children entertained while adults settle in for tea, coffee and a chat, with high chairs and baby chairs on hand for the littlest visitors. The group also marks the calendar with parties for Halloween, Easter and other holidays. Cost is €3 per child.

Also known as the Little Buddies Toddler Group, Abbeyquarter Parent and Toddler Group meets in a warm, friendly setting at The Avalon Centre on Chapel Street, Abbeyquarter North, Sligo. Sessions run every Wednesday during the school term, 10am to 11.30am.

It's a good way for parents and children alike to make new connections - little ones get to socialise while adults can pick up parenting tips and support from each other. Tea, coffee, biscuits and snacks for the kids are all provided. Cost is €5 per family; call 071 916 1836 for more details.

Ballintrillick Parent and Toddler Group meets every Tuesday during the school term, 10am to 12pm, at The Benwiskin Centre in Gortnahoula, Co. Sligo. Staff prepare the hall in advance with chairs and toys and take care of cleaning and sanitising everything afterwards, giving children a safe, comfortable space to play while parents and guardians supervise and get to know one another.

Tea, coffee and biscuits are on offer for adults, with juice for the children, and the centre keeps a microwave, nappy changing table, potty, baby swing chair and a breastfeeding cushion on hand. The €3 family fee is paid weekly on the day rather than online. Contact the school on 071 917 6721 for more information.

Hosted by Ballymote Family Resource Centre and also known as the Peek-A-Boo Baby and Toddler Group, this session takes place every Wednesday during the school term from 10am to 12pm at the centre on the corner of Wolfe Tone Street and Keash Road, Co. Sligo.

There's a good range of toys plus a dedicated sensory room for children to explore, while mums, dads and caregivers settle in for a cuppa and a chat. It's free to attend - call 098 21446 for more information.

Mucky Monday Tots is the toddler session run by Sligo Children's Community Garden, meeting every Monday from 10.30am to 12pm at The Avalon Centre, Chapel Street, Abbeyquarter North, Sligo. It's a hands-on morning of muddy, messy garden play - planting seeds, digging in the soil, and simply getting outside together.

Expect laughter, fresh air and a cup of tea while young nature enthusiasts get stuck in. Cost is €3 per family; email sligochildrenscommunitygarden@gmail.com to find out more.

Geevagh/Highwood Parent and Toddler Group welcomes families to a fun, friendly session at Geevagh Resource Centre, Co. Sligo, every Wednesday during the school term from 10am to 11.30am. Parents and carers stay with their children throughout, trading a bit of adult company and coffee while the little ones play.

Over the summer months the group also organises buggy walks, so it's worth keeping an eye on their social media for updates. Cost is €5 for the first child and €1 for each additional child; call 087 978 0077 for details.

First Steps Parent and Toddler Group meets at Sligo Methodist Church on Wine Street every Thursday during the school term, 10.15am to 11.45am, and is open to all preschool children accompanied by a parent or guardian.

Drop in for a cup of tea while the children enjoy books, toys and colouring - there's something to keep every little one occupied. The session is free to attend; call 087 913 7713 for more information.

Sligo Family Resource Centre on The Mall runs its Parent and Toddler Group twice a week during the school term, every Tuesday and Wednesday from 10.30am to 11.30am. Facilitators lead a programme of music, drama and messy play designed to build toddlers' language and movement skills, followed by tea, coffee and healthy snacks.

The group is linked to an associated drama group, and the year includes an annual Christmas party with Santa in December and a summer picnic to Doorly Park in June. It's free to attend. The centre also runs a regular Dads' Group where fathers can share their experiences of fatherhood - check the centre's social media for upcoming dates.

The ImagiNation is a colourful, screen-free role play mini world at Lyons Department Store on O'Connell Street, Sligo, designed for toddlers, preschoolers and children up to age 7 - tiny tag-alongs are welcome too. Children explore real-life role play zones including a café, supermarket, vets, salon and emergency services, with play that's child-led, open-ended and geared towards building confidence, communication, social skills and imagination.

Bookable sessions run through the week and on Saturdays, alongside private birthday parties and school or group bookings. A small baby area is set aside for younger siblings, and caregivers stay for the duration with seating and clear visibility across the play space. Pricing is €15 per child and €10 per sibling, with a pre-walker sibling rate also available.

Comfortable clothes and socks are all that's needed - no special equipment required, just curiosity and imagination.

Tubbercurry Parent and Toddler Group is run by Tubbercurry Family Resource Centre on the Mountain Road, meeting every Monday during the school term from 10.30am to 12.30pm. It's a drop-in session, so there's no need to book - just pop along.

The morning takes in sing-songs, painting, sensory play, stacking and sorting games, afternoon tea and the occasional guest speaker, with new parents always made welcome. Cost is €2 per family; contact the centre on 071 91 86926.

This 5-week Baby Yoga course at Yoga Nenagh Studio is suitable for babies from around 8 weeks old up to crawling age (10 weeks if recovering from a C-section). Each class runs for about 30 minutes on Saturday mornings, 10am to 11am, and focuses on co-regulation and nurturing the bond between parent and baby.

All mats and equipment are supplied, and the group heads to a local café for light refreshments after each session - included in the €100 booking fee. Spaces are limited, so early booking is recommended.

Borrisokane Parent, Baby and Toddler Group meets at the Silver Arch FRC Outreach Office every Wednesday during term time, from 10am to 11am. It's a welcoming setting where babies and toddlers can play together on mats and with toys while caregivers catch up over tea or coffee.

A €2 contribution covers the session. Call 067 31800 or check the group's Facebook page for details - and keep an eye on social media after school holidays, as the restart date doesn't always align exactly with term time.

Also known as Tiny Tots Playgroup, Carrick-on-Suir Parent, Baby and Toddler Group meets every Tuesday during the school term from 10am to 11.30am at the Community Resource Centre in Greenside, Co. Tipperary. Children enjoy play, activities, songs and stories, while parents, guardians, carers and grandparents get tea, coffee and a chance to chat.

Cost is €3 per family; call 051 642 418 for more information.

The Wandering Mothers is a walking group for mums and their babies, meeting outside Fetch Coffee on The Quay in Clonmel every Thursday at 9.30am during the warmer months. The route follows the blueway and back, roughly 5km in total, with some of the group staying on afterwards for a coffee or treat.

Numbers are confirmed the night before via a WhatsApp poll, so it's worth joining the group to stay in the loop - message thesaucysoul-coachingstudio on Instagram or fill out the form in the bio to be added. Day and time can shift, so keep an eye on updates. It's free to join.

Gentle Touch Baby Massage with Roisin brings a 5-week baby massage course to Roscrea, giving new parents a chance to learn massage strokes for their baby while meeting other parents in the area.

The course costs €125, and many health insurance plans allow up to €100 of that to be claimed back.

Glengoole Parent, Baby and Toddler Group is hosted by Millennium Family Resource Centre in New Birmingham, Thurles, meeting every Thursday during the school term from 10.30am to 12pm. It's an easy-going morning for parents to meet others in the area while babies and toddlers make friends and explore new toys.

A small contribution is asked for; call 083 207 1368 or check the group's Facebook page for updates.

Knockanrawley Parent, Baby and Toddler Group is run by Knockanrawley Resource Centre every Thursday from 10.30am to 11.30am. Sessions include sensory toys, artwork and small world play, alongside plenty of opportunity for children to play alongside others their own age and for parents to meet people locally.

Spaces are limited, so registration is required in advance - call 083 423 8915 to book. It's free to attend.

Run entirely by volunteers, Lattin-Cullen Parent, Baby and Toddler Group meets every Wednesday during the school term from 9.30am to 11am at Hannon GAA Park, home of Lattin-Cullen GAA Club. There's a good supply of toys and a warm welcome for newcomers looking to meet people and let the kids burn off some energy.

Cost is €3 per family; call 085 720 7002 for details. Note that the group doesn't run any social media, so phone is the best way to check in.

Monard Parent, Baby and Toddler Group meets every Friday during the school term, 9.30am to 11.30am, at Monard Community Hall in Co. Tipperary. Snacks are provided, though parents are asked to bring along a drink for their child, and there's a good selection of toys to keep babies and toddlers entertained while they meet others their own age.

New faces are always welcome, with fresh activities added regularly. Cost is €5 per family; call 086 366 7624 or check the group's Facebook page for more.

Nenagh Parent, Baby and Toddler Group, run by Silver Arch Family Resource Centre, meets at Tyone Community Centre every Friday during the school term from 10am to 11.30am. It's a drop-in session, so there's no obligation to attend every week - toddlers get a chance to socialise with plenty of toys and mats on hand, while the grown-ups can enjoy a cup of tea.

Cost is a €2 contribution; call 067 31800 or check the Facebook page, bearing in mind the restart after school holidays doesn't always match the term calendar exactly.

Roscrea Parent, Baby and Toddler Group meets every Thursday during the school term, 9.30am to 10.30am, at Scoil Iosef Naofa in Corville, Co. Tipperary. Mums, dads, grandparents and childminders are all welcome to pop along with their little one - there's no need to sign up for a term, and plenty of toys to keep children entertained while they get used to playing alongside others their age.

It's free to attend; contact Lisa on 086 191 3383 or find the group on Facebook.

Sensory Play Studio offers sensory play classes for children from around 4 months old, built around child-led play in a 'yes' environment where kids are free to explore the toys and resources however they like. Sessions are stay-and-play, so grown-ups can join in, observe, or simply relax with a tea or coffee while their child gets stuck in.

Options include pay-as-you-go sessions, a dedicated neurodivergent class, a Mom & Baby term, a Messy Baby term, and a 6-week Sensory Club block, with pricing to suit different levels of commitment. Old clothes are recommended for every class, and class t-shirts or jumpers are available to purchase.

Templemore Parent, Baby and Toddler Group welcomes parents and caregivers with babies and toddlers from birth up to ECCE preschool age, meeting every Wednesday morning during the school term from 10am to 11.30am. Find the group at Templemore Community Preschool (look for the green gate), E41 F3P3, where there's a good stock of toys and games plus refreshments for the adults.

The group occasionally runs special sessions such as first aid classes, and organises a buggy walk over the summer. A €2 contribution towards materials and refreshments is appreciated; call 083 160 6832 or check Facebook for updates.

Run by Silver Arch Family Resource Centre, Thurles Parent, Baby and Toddler Group meets every Tuesday during the school term from 10.30am to 11.30am at The Source Arts Centre on Cathedral Street. It operates on a pop-in basis, so there's no pressure to attend every week - babies and toddlers get to play and interact while parents enjoy a cup of tea and a chat.

A €2 contribution covers the session; call 067 31800 or check the Facebook page, and note the restart date after school holidays can vary slightly from the term calendar.

Three Drives Family Resource Centre hosts two weekly groups for local families at 22/23 Greenane Drive, Tipperary Town. The Parent and Toddler Group meets each week as a chance to connect with other parents and carers in the community, share tips, and let children join in games and play together.

Alongside it, a Breastfeeding Support Group runs weekly for mums who are breastfeeding, have new babies, or are considering breastfeeding, offering peer support while babies and young toddlers play together. Both are free to attend - call 062 80831 or check the centre's Facebook page to book your place.

Zen Baby by Grace runs a 5-week baby massage course at On Your Toes Dance Studio on the Fethard Road, Clonmel - a relaxed way for parents to bond with their infant while meeting other new parents.

Booking is essential, as spaces are limited; call 086 377 0022 to reserve a place.

Clashmore/Kinsalebeg Parent, Baby and Toddler Group meets every second Tuesday during the school term, 10am to 12pm, at Clashmore Kinsalebeg GAA Club in Raheen, Co. Waterford. All are welcome to drop in for tea or coffee and a chat, with plenty of toys, books and games to keep babies and toddlers busy.

Cost is €5 per adult; find the group's contact details via its social media accounts.

Creation Cup runs a 6-week Kids Art Fusion course for young artists aged 5 to 11, held on Saturdays at Garter Lane Studio in Waterford. Sessions are built around creative, hands-on projects that help develop self-esteem, focus and resilience through art.

The course costs €120; book a place by direct message or via the online form.

Messy Munchkins by Jen runs hands-on messy play sessions every Tuesday from 10.30am to 11.30am at Cheekpoint Community Hall on the Crossroad, Co. Waterford. Activities are designed to stimulate toddlers' senses and creativity, and caregivers - mums, dads, grandparents or childminders - are asked to stay for the full session, making it a nice chance to bond together over the mess.

A term of 4 weeks costs €40, or sessions can be booked pay-as-you-go from €12.50. Materials are all provided, though it's worth dressing children in clothes that can get messy and packing a change just in case. Weekend sessions are also available for ages 3 to 6 - get in touch for more details.

Ballymoney Steiner Kindergarten and Preschool hosts a Parent and Toddler group in its child-centred rooms, meeting every Thursday during the school term from 9.30am to 11.30am in Kiltennel, Gorey. Children get to explore toys and play with others in a calm, Steiner-inspired setting, and the entrance fee includes a healthy snack and hot drink for adults.

Fees start from €8 per family; email ballymoneysteiner@gmail.com to find out more or arrange a first visit.

Bree Parent, Baby and Toddler Group meets every Tuesday during the school term, 10.30am to 12pm, at Bree Community Centre near Enniscorthy. It's open to parents, grandparents, childminders and children from babies through to wobblers and toddlers, and sessions are drop-in with no need to book ahead.

Cost is from €2 per family. Contact Ruth on 085 118 0930 or Alice on 085 229 5817 - phone is the best way to reach the group, as its social media isn't actively updated.

Bunclody Library runs a full programme of free sessions for children of all ages. Rhymetime brings stories, songs and rhymes for 0 to 5 year olds every Wednesday at 11.15am, while Storytime for ages 4 to 7 runs every Saturday at 11am (book a space for the child only).

For a quieter visit, the library's Sensory Friendly Hour offers a calm environment every Saturday from 4pm to 5pm, and teens aged 13 to 15 can join the Young Adult Book Club on the first Friday of each month, 4.15pm to 5pm.

Bunclody Parent, Baby and Toddler Group meets every Thursday during the school term, 9.30am to 11am, at the Pastoral Centre attached to Most Holy Trinity Church on Main Street. It's a welcoming spot for parents, carers and grandparents to meet over a cup of tea while children play, take part in activities and enjoy some songs.

Cost is €3 per family. The group keeps a private Facebook page for planned activities - contact Catherine on 083 321 9929 to get involved.

Craanford Parent, Baby and Toddler Group runs a playgroup for babies, wobblers, toddlers and preschoolers at Craanford Community Centre every second Thursday during the school term, 10.30am to 12.30pm. It's a drop-in morning where parents and carers can meet new people while the children play and make friends.

Cost is €4 per family; contact Carol on 087 288 9917 for more information.

Enniscorthy Library runs a full slate of free weekly activities for children and teens. Rhyme Time gathers little ones for songs and rhymes every Wednesday at 11am, followed by Story Time on Saturdays at 11am for slightly older children.

There's also a Junior Chess Club on Wednesdays from 3.30pm to 4.30pm, Lego Free Play running Saturdays from 11am to 3pm, and a Young Adult Book Club meeting Wednesdays from 4pm to 5pm - something for nearly every age group across the week.

Gorey Library offers a varied programme for babies and kids throughout the month. Baby and Toddler Storytime runs every Tuesday at 11am, while Lego Freeplay takes over on Saturdays from 10.30am to 12.30pm.

Families looking for something different can join the Parent and Toddler Rhyme and Song Time held in Ukrainian on the second Wednesday of each month at 10.30am, or Sensory Play sessions on the third Monday of the month at 11am.

Gorey Parent, Baby and Toddler Group meets every Tuesday during the school term, 10am to 12pm, in a colourful, well-equipped playroom at Gorey Youth Needs Group on St Michael's Road. It's run informally by parents themselves with support from GYNG staff, welcoming children from newborn right up to school-going age, along with their parents, childminders or grandparents.

There's no charge to join, though donations towards tea, coffee and refreshments are appreciated. New members are always welcome; call 053 942 2611 for details.

Lullababy Baby Classes runs a range of term-based sessions for babies at An Seomra, Room 23, Gorey Business Park. Baby Massage classes suit babies from birth to 12 months and run over 6 weeks, while Baby Reflexology follows a 5-week term for the same age range - both sessions last 90 minutes and typically start at 10am.

For slightly older babies, Baby Yoga is suited to those from around 12 weeks up to pre-crawling age, running as a 4-week term.

Southend Family Resource Centre runs the Maudlintown Parent, Baby and Toddler Group every Thursday during the school term, 9.30am to 11.30am, at its base on Hantoon Road, just off Maudlintown Green and opposite the Senator Windows building. The aim is to give parents a supportive space away from their own four walls while children play safely together.

Each week brings a different activity for the toddlers - painting, puppet making, baking, or time outdoors when the weather allows - alongside healthy snacks for the kids and tea and coffee for the grown-ups. Parents also pick up informal support and information on courses, training and other services available through the centre. Cost is a voluntary €2 per family contribution; contact Siobhan on 087 763 3002.
New Ross Library runs a free Rhymetime session every Thursday at 11am - a fun-packed half hour of stories, rhymes and songs for babies and young children.

New Ross Parent, Baby and Toddler Group meets every Friday during the school term, 9.30am to 11am, at Youth New Ross on The Bullawn. It's an easy way for parents to meet for tea, coffee and a chat while the children play - no registration or sign-up needed, just drop in.

It's free to attend, with donations welcome. For more information, contact Lauren or Hayley at info@ynr.ie or call the office on 051 425 415, extension 16.

North Wexford Parent and Toddler Group meets every Tuesday morning, 10am to 11.30am, in the Viewing Gallery at KCC, Kilanerin. It's a voluntary, non-profit group run by parents for parents, built around building a support network and sharing tips in a relaxed setting.

A soft play area with a bouncy castle and ball pit gives babies and toddlers plenty of room to explore, and the €3 fee covers room hire along with tea and coffee for the adults.

Ramsgrange Parent, Baby and Toddler Group is hosted by South West Wexford Family Resource Centre every Tuesday during the school term, 10am to 12pm, and is aimed at children from birth to 4 years old. Parents get the chance to chat and compare notes on their child's development while the kids play and socialise with a wide range of toys and equipment, with a sing-song built into each session and a staff member on hand to facilitate.

Cost is €3 per family, and new members are always welcome; contact Sinead on 087 360 5595.

Rathnure Parent, Baby and Toddler Group gives parents, fathers and minders a chance to get out of the house while children get some playtime with others their own age, meeting every Friday during the school term from 9.30am to 11.15am at Rathnure National School.

Expect fun, games and plenty of laughter, with lots of toys on hand. Cost is €2 per family; contact Emma on 086 842 8848.

Also known as Little Steps Playgroup, Rosslare Parent, Baby and Toddler Group meets every Thursday during the school term, 9.30am to 11am, at Rosslare Community & Sports Centre. Sessions are drop-in, welcoming babies right through to preschoolers, with toys and plenty of space to play in the hall.

The group occasionally puts on special events like puppet shows or face painting, and always welcomes new members and holiday visitors. Cost is €2 per family; contact Maria on 053 913 2202.

Taghmon Parent, Baby and Toddler Group is hosted by Taghmon Family Resource Centre on Joseph Street every Thursday during the school term, 9.30am to 11am, for parents, grandparents, foster parents and childminders with children aged 0 to 4. Sessions include sensory activities alongside the usual chat and play, and the group marks the year with seasonal events such as Santa visits and trips to local castles.

It's free to attend, with donations welcome; contact Emma on 053 913 4465.

Toddle On is a play café based in DB Fitness and Injuries, Unit 5 Pinewood Business Park (beside Lidl in Clonard), Wexford, with a play space suitable for children aged 0 to 10 and themed sensory and messy play classes for those aged roughly 2 months to 6 years. The site is split into four rooms: a calm Sensory Play Room for babies and toddlers with soft play, lights and textures; an Imaginative Play Room for role-play and dress-up; a Creative & Messy Play Classroom for hands-on projects; and a Games Room where older siblings can enjoy basketball, mini snooker and imaginative play.

Classes are grouped by age: Toddle On Teenies focuses on baby sensory, baby beats, Lámh and baby massage; Toddle On Tinies builds on sensory play, Lámh, messy play and music with instruments; and Toddle On Tots layers in messy play, role play, stories, numeracy, Lámh, music and crafts around a weekly theme.

Drop-in play sessions can be used any time within opening hours on the day booked, and all caregivers are required to stay for the duration. All resources are provided, refreshments are available to buy, and sibling discounts and memberships are on offer. It's worth bringing an easily removable outfit for baby classes and avoiding new clothes for the messier sessions.

Birthday parties are also available, with full use of the play space and a bubble disco for €100, plus optional snack bags to use as party favours.

Down Syndrome Wexford's Parent and Toddler Group, also known as 3-2-1 Tots, supports parents of preschool-aged children with a playgroup held every second Sunday morning during term time at Craanford Community Centre. Little ones get to play together in a relaxed, understanding setting.

The group runs an active Instagram account that can be requested to join for further details, and it's free to attend; contact David on 086 333 2845.

Wexford Town Library keeps a busy weekly calendar for children and young people of all ages. Younger visitors can join Rhyme Time on Wednesdays at 11am or Story Time on Saturdays at 11am, while older kids might prefer the Junior Chess Club (Wednesdays, 3.30-4.30pm) or Lego Free Play (Saturdays, 11am-3pm).

Teenagers are catered for too, with a Young Adult Book Club meeting every Wednesday from 4pm to 5pm. All sessions are free to attend, and no booking is generally required beyond turning up on the day.

Enniskerry Parent & Toddler Group meets every Thursday during the school term, 9.15am to 11am, at the Parish Hall beside Poppies on Main Street, Enniskerry. Mums-to-be, parents and carers are all welcome to bring along babies, toddlers and preschoolers for some free playtime while the adults catch up over a cup of coffee.

Cost is a modest €1.50 per family.

Leopardstown Lawn Tennis Club runs a Junior Tennis Development Programme for children and teens aged 5 to 18, held across floodlit outdoor courts at the club in Leopardstown, Dublin 18. Sessions run most days of the week, Monday to Saturday, starting from 2pm, and take players from complete beginners through to competitive standard.

Junior coaching is included as part of club membership, while individual private lessons are also available separately with coaches at different levels, priced from roughly €35 to €70 an hour depending on experience. Free parking is available on-site at this long-established, family-oriented club.

West Wood Club's Summer Tennis Camp runs Monday to Friday for children aged 6 to 10, held inside Ireland's largest indoor tennis centre at Leopardstown Racecourse in Foxrock. The week combines coaching, games and skill-building aimed at young beginner-to-intermediate players.

The venue has a café and changing facilities on-site along with free parking, and members can take advantage of early-booking discounts on camp fees - non-member pricing is confirmed at the time of booking.

Donnybrook Lawn Tennis Club offers a welcoming, inclusive environment where children of all ages and skill levels can enjoy and improve their tennis. The Junior Programme balances social and competitive play through regular events such as Super Saturdays, Round Robin tournaments, Play & Pizza nights and inter-club matches, with additional sessions organised around tournament or league match practice as needed.

During school breaks the club runs junior tennis camps in February, at Easter and over the summer, while the Junior Club Championships in late August provide a highlight of the year for young players to compete and mark their progress.

Rathgar Tennis Club offers a fun, safe and supportive environment for children and teenagers of all ages and abilities. Junior members get year-round coaching, the chance to make friends and stay active, led by coach Jamie Pilkington and his team through a Junior Programme that follows the school calendar with three terms of group lessons each year.

Younger players benefit from the ITF Tennis 10s approach, using short courts and low-bounce balls to help skills develop more easily. Lessons are tailored by age and ability, and older juniors can progress into one of three squad groups for extra coaching, with up to eight hours of weekly training available.

Stratford LTC offers year-round junior coaching for children aged 5 and up, on four floodlit all-weather courts with access to four grass courts during the summer. Lessons are grouped by age and skill level and run in 6-week blocks that follow the school year, focusing on technique, drills and gameplay.

Each 60-minute session uses the ITF Tennis 10s system, with red, orange and green balls supporting players as their skills develop. Summer camps take the place of weekly lessons during school holidays, and all coaches are experienced, Garda vetted and trained in child safeguarding.

Columbus Club runs summer camps for kids at its premises on Leeson Street Lower, Dublin 2, offering a break-time programme of activities during the school holidays.

Contact the club directly for the current summer camp schedule, age groups and booking details.

Complete Harmony runs Toddler Yoga classes for children aged 18 months to 5 years, with parents attending alongside their child. Sessions take place in person at The Quaker Meeting House in Churchtown, Dublin 14, or online via Zoom for those who prefer to join from home.

A block of 6 classes starts from €135.

Dublin Tomiki Aikido runs a Junior Aikido programme for children aged 6 to 9 at Belgard Youth & Community Centre in Tallaght. Classes take place twice a week, Tuesdays from 5pm to 6pm and Saturdays from 9.30am to 10.30am, giving young beginners a structured introduction to the discipline, focus and coordination that aikido builds.

Fees run to approximately €50 a month.

DublinArtClasses.com runs a range of after-school and ongoing art programmes for kids and teens at Balgriffin Hall on the Malahide Road, Dublin 13, including the Little Da Vinci's programme for children aged 8 to 12. Classes are kept small, with a maximum of 12 children, giving each young artist plenty of room to develop their own style and technique.

JSBJJ Training Centre offers Kids Brazilian Jiu Jitsu at its Parnell Street premises in Dublin, with age-specific classes for 4-6 year olds, 7-10 year olds, and a Teens group for 11-13 year olds. Grouping by age lets instructors pitch techniques and games to where each stage of development is at, from early coordination and discipline through to more technical grappling for older kids.

Mini Music runs early years music classes for babies and children aged 3 months to 5 years, held at the Churchtown School of Music on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays, with an additional Saturday class at the National Concert Hall. Sessions introduce young children to rhythm, singing and movement in a setting built around their stage of development.

The Ark on Eustace Street in Temple Bar is Dublin's dedicated cultural centre for children, running a programme of creative arts activities alongside family-friendly exhibitions and theatre productions throughout the year.

Among its offerings is a free visual arts exhibition designed specifically for babies, making it one of the few cultural spaces in the city geared towards the very youngest visitors as well as older children.

Christ City Church runs a free Summer Kids Club called 'Brave Adventurers' for primary school-aged children at Lindsay Road National School in Glasnevin, held over a week in July from 9.30am to 12pm each day.

It's a no-cost option for families looking for a morning activity during the summer break - contact the church for the current year's dates and booking details.

codingclasses.ie runs after-school coding, robotics and digital literacy programmes for children and teens aged 7 to 18, held across several school venues around Dublin. Classes are structured to build practical tech skills progressively, from early programming concepts for younger kids through to more advanced robotics and coding challenges for teens.

Aoife Burke School of Drama runs after-school drama classes in Rathfarnham on Fridays and Ballinteer on Saturdays, with groups organised by age and experience: Tiny Tots for 3 to 5 year olds, Juniors from age 6 up, and Intermediate and Teens groups for older students.

Drama classes at this age typically build confidence, imagination and communication skills through games, improvisation and performance, giving children a structured path to grow into more advanced work as they progress through the groups.

Dublin Kendo runs a Kids Kendo class for children aged 8 to 16 every Saturday from 1.30pm to 3.30pm at Ballybough Community Youth & Sports Centre, Dublin 3. The traditional Japanese martial art builds discipline, focus and physical coordination through bamboo sword practice and structured drills.

A free trial session is offered on the first Saturday of each month for anyone wanting to try before committing.

This CoderDojo chapter, hosted at Leman Solicitors on Percy Place in Ballsbridge, is a free, volunteer-led coding club for children and teens aged 7 to 17. Sessions run on Saturdays, and a parent or guardian is required to stay on site for the duration.

As part of the global CoderDojo network, the club follows a mentor-led, self-paced approach that lets young coders work on projects at their own level, from first steps in programming through to more advanced builds.

Littleroo runs a range of toddler-and-family programmes around Dublin, including Toddler Ballet classes, messy play sessions, and family and holiday-themed events throughout the year.

Get in touch for current class locations, schedules and booking details.

Musicologie Junior offers experiential music classes for children aged 6 months to 5 years in Dublin, with each 40-minute session blending singing, movement, instruments and read-along books.

The multi-sensory format is designed to introduce young children to music through active participation rather than passive listening, building early rhythm and listening skills as they grow.

School Kids Aloud runs full-day summer camps for children aged 5 to 12 across three Dublin locations - Phoenix Park, Pelletstown and Luttrelstown - with long opening hours from 8am to 6pm to suit working parents.

The camps qualify for National Childcare Scheme (NCS) subsidy support, helping to offset the cost for eligible families.

Timprov runs beginner-friendly improv courses at Carleton Hall in Marino, built around confidence-building, listening skills and spontaneous storytelling. The 6-week Learn Improv course introduces the fundamentals of improvisational theatre through games and group exercises, giving young performers a low-pressure way to build stage confidence.

Total Ninja is home to Dublin's largest indoor ninja-style obstacle course, with a dedicated Little Ninja programme scaled down for younger children to tackle age-appropriate obstacles safely.

Beyond regular sessions, the venue also hosts family days and birthday parties, making it a popular option for active celebrations as well as weekly training.

Viva Kids Ballet runs small-group ballet classes for children aged 3 to 5 at Viva School in Fairview, Dublin 3. Sessions last 60 minutes and take place every Tuesday from 6pm to 7pm, giving young dancers an early introduction to posture, movement and basic ballet positions in a small-class setting.

Fees are €50 a month.

Circus Factory Cork's Thursday Youth Circus introduces children aged 7 to 11 to circus skills including juggling, hula-hoop, acrobatics and aerial arts, held at Centre Park House in Cork City. Each session runs for an hour and fifteen minutes, giving young performers time to build coordination, strength and confidence across a range of disciplines.

All tutors are Garda vetted.

Cork Judo Club runs judo sessions for all ages at Cobh Great Island Community Centre, with a dedicated kids class for 5 to 16 year olds every Thursday from 6pm to 7pm.

Judo builds balance, discipline and physical confidence through structured throws, grappling and falling technique, taught in a club setting that also welcomes adult members.

Cork Sports Partnership's Try Track & Field programme gives children aged 7 and up a free, 8-week introduction to athletics at Bunscoil Rinn An Chabhlaigh in Cobh. Beginner coaching covers the basics of running, jumping and throwing, with sessions starting Wednesdays from 7pm to 8pm.

It's a low-cost way for kids to try a range of track and field disciplines before committing to a club.

Cove Sailing Club has run junior sailing at Whitepoint, Cobh, since 2009, with a dedicated dinghy fleet and qualified instructors teaching young sailors on Cork Harbour. Three sessions run each Saturday, giving junior members regular time on the water to build skills and confidence.

The long-running programme has become an established part of the sailing calendar in Cobh.

Krav Junior at Institute Krav Maga Cork introduces children and teens to practical self-defence in a safe, structured environment, building confidence and fitness alongside core Krav Maga techniques.

A free trial class is available for anyone wanting to try a session before signing up.

SailCork's Junior Courses cover sailing, powerboating, rafting and kayaking for children aged 4 to 16 at East Ferry Marina in Cobh. Weekly Saturday sessions run alongside holiday camps, giving young water-sports enthusiasts a chance to try a broad mix of activities on Cork Harbour throughout the year.

Studio Wolfe runs kids dance classes for ages 3 to 12 across three Cork locations - Douglas, Donnybrook and Blarney - with dancers progressing from the beginner Little Stars group through Junior and Intermediate levels as their skills develop.

Fees start from €155 per term.

Declan O'Meara Art runs kids art and craft classes for ages 5 to 12 at Lough Scouts Hall on Lough Road, Cork City, led by a qualified art teacher. The programme covers a broad mix of disciplines including painting, drawing, ceramics and jewellery-making, giving children the chance to explore different materials and techniques across the term.

The Yoga Nook's Kids Yoga Adventures in Cork introduces children aged 4 to 9 to yoga through storytelling-based movement, cooperative games and simple mindfulness exercises alongside poses that build strength and balance.

The playful, story-led format is designed to keep younger children engaged while still building the focus and body awareness that yoga practice offers.

Stage School Limerick runs weekly dance, drama and singing classes at St Munchins Community Enterprise Centre in Kileely, led by Ciara Sexton, who has performed with Riverdance, alongside Orielle O'Donnell. The combined format gives children a broad grounding across performing arts disciplines rather than focusing on just one, building confidence on stage as much as technical skill.

Limerick Print Makers runs kids art classes during school terms for two age groups, 5 to 8 and 9 to 12, at its studio on John's Square. The programme covers printmaking, clay work, painting and drawing, giving children hands-on experience across several art forms.

Single-day workshops and summer camps are also available outside of term time for those looking for a one-off session or holiday activity.

Limerick School of Acting runs kids' and teens' acting classes led by Nigel Mercier, with sessions on Saturdays at St Michael's Hall on Pery Square and Sundays at Kilmurry Arts Centre. Students aged 6 to 18 are grouped by age and experience, giving each level material suited to where they're at, from first steps in acting through to more advanced technique for older teens.

Limerick School of Classical Ballet runs term-based ballet classes from Pre-Primary right through to Grade 5 and above, plus a Jazz option, across two locations: the Redemptorist Studio on Tuesdays and Saturdays, and Castletroy on Fridays and Sundays.

Fees start from €155 per term, with grading giving dancers a clear pathway to progress as their technique develops.

Tiger Academy's Limerick Shojinkai runs junior beginners karate for children aged 4 to 8 at the Dooradoyle Dojo, based at Garryowen Rugby Club. Classes run Mondays and Wednesdays from 5pm to 5.30pm, plus Fridays from 5.30pm to 6pm, giving young beginners a structured, age-appropriate introduction to karate.

A 3-month block costs €130.

Little Kickers Limerick runs football classes for children aged 18 months to 8 years, split across four age-specific programmes at venues including Raheen, Gaelscoil Raheen and Groody Road. Classes run for 49 weeks of the year, giving young players a consistent, near-continuous programme to build football skills and confidence as they move up through each age band.

Little Stars Music School runs group music classes for children aged 1 to 6 from September to June, led by Sarah O'Kennedy, who trained through both ABRSM and Trinity College London. Classes at the school's base in Annacotty focus on rhythm, pitch and early notation, giving young children a solid grounding in musical fundamentals before they move on to a specific instrument.

Dance Academy Limerick, based at Castletroy Town Centre, offers ballet, jazz/lyrical and tap for children aged 3 and up, starting with creative dance for 3 year olds before moving into formal ballet training from age 4.

Dancers can progress along exam and competition pathways as their technique develops, giving families the option to pursue dance recreationally or more competitively.

Claire Halpin Yoga and Pilates runs Kids Yoga & Mindfulness classes for children aged 4 to 12 in Limerick, combining breathwork, yoga games and non-competitive instruction.

The relaxed, pressure-free approach is designed to help children build focus and body awareness through play rather than formal poses alone.

Genevieve Ryan Dance Academy runs toddler-friendly dance classes for children aged 3 to 5, split into two programmes: Twinkle Toes, a ballet-focused class, and Happy Feet, which blends creative movement, musical theatre and hip hop.

Both classes are designed around the shorter attention spans and energy levels typical of this age group, keeping young dancers engaged through variety and play.

Little Trickers, the Galway branch of Little Kickers, runs pre-school football classes for children aged 18 months to 5 years across multiple venues in Galway. Coaches are Garda vetted, and a free trial class is available for families wanting to try a session before signing up.

Classes at this age focus on basic coordination, following instructions and simple ball skills through games rather than structured drills.

Emer MacDermott Art School runs kids art classes for all ages at a child-centred studio in Corrandulla, with sessions on Wednesdays and Thursdays from 4.30pm to 6pm, and Saturdays from midday to 1.30pm.

Fees are €65 a month, with a one-off €25 signup charge for new students.

Galway Art Academy's Afterschool Art Club runs weekly art classes for children aged 7 to 12 at two venues - Gaelscoil Mhic Amhlaigh in Knocknacarra and Scoil Áinde BNS in Salthill - with sessions held on Tuesdays and Thursdays respectively.

The afterschool format lets children extend their creative skills straight after the school day, without needing a separate trip across town.

Galway Martial Arts Academy runs children's martial arts programmes for ages 4 to 15, split into three groups tailored to developmental stage: Pandas for 4 to 6 year olds, Tigers for 7 to 10 year olds, and Dragons for 11 to 15 year olds.

Grading students this way lets instructors pitch coordination work, discipline and technique to what's appropriate for each age band, rather than teaching a single mixed-age class.

Phonics with Robot Reg runs early literacy classes in Galway for children aged 3 months to 5 years, combining phonics with play, music and movement to introduce early reading skills in a hands-on, age-appropriate way.

A 3-week trial is available for families wanting to try the format before committing to a longer term.

Sara Falvey Yoga runs Kids Yoga for children aged 6 and up every Monday from 3.45pm to 4.35pm at Yoga Darsana, based at the Old Driving Range in Salthill, Galway.

Classes are drop-in at €12 per session, making it an easy option to try without committing to a full term upfront.

Motiv8 runs youth-focused gym classes for ages 11 to 16 in Waterford, taught in a small-group format by coaches trained to support neurodiverse needs alongside general strength and fitness coaching for teens.

A 5-class pack costs €75.

SEA School Saturdays runs hands-on nature-based science and art activities for children aged 7 to 15, held every Saturday from 10am to 1pm at Tramore Coastguard Cultural Centre in Dunmore East. Sessions blend coastal and marine themes with creative and scientific exploration.

Cost is €25 per session.

Waterford Gymnastics runs Parent & Toddler classes for children aged 1 to 5 at its base in Carrickpherish Business Park, with sessions on Sundays at 10am and 11.15am, plus Mondays at 10am. Each hour-long class combines soft play with proper gym equipment, giving toddlers an early, supervised introduction to movement and coordination alongside a parent or carer.

Waterford Youth Arts runs contemporary dance workshops at The Arch on Barrack Street, led by Izzy Carr, with separate sessions for ages 6 to 8 on Thursdays at 4.30pm and ages 9 to 11 on Thursdays at 5.30pm.

Fees are €45 per term, with family discounts available for households sending more than one child.

Freedom Surf School runs Billabong-branded surf camps for kids and teens in Tramore, with age-specific groups covering roughly 6 to 17 year olds. Camps run over the summer and Easter school holidays, with all surfing equipment provided as part of the package.

Grouping by age lets instructors match wave conditions and coaching pace to each group's ability and confidence in the water.

Camp Waterford runs multi-activity day camps at Newtown School's 18-acre site, which includes an indoor pool, with weekly camps throughout July. Younger children aged 4 to 6 join Cub Camp, while Camp Waterford proper caters for ages 7 to 15 with a broader range of activities across the site.

The scale of the grounds and facilities allows for a wide mix of sports, water-based activity and outdoor play across the camp week.

Tramore Code Club is a free, volunteer-led coding club for children and teens aged 7 to 17, meeting on Saturdays from 4pm to 5.45pm during term time at Gaelscoil Philib Barúin. It's part of the global Code Club network, which supports young people learning to code through structured, self-paced projects delivered by volunteer mentors.

Dungarvan Gymnastics Club offers both recreational and competitive gymnastics for children aged 4 and up, with classes running Tuesday to Saturday. The club is affiliated with Gymnastics Ireland, giving competitive gymnasts a clear pathway into regional and national events as they progress.

Dungarvan School of Music and Trad offers instrumental lessons in guitar, tin whistle and bodhrán, alongside a Children's Choir split into two age groups - 5 to 8 and 9 to 17 - and Irish dance classes.

The mix of instrumental tuition, singing and dance gives families a range of traditional and contemporary options to choose from under one school.

GOMA Gallery runs children's art classes led by Ben Hennessy every Saturday, with separate groups for ages 4 to 6 and 7 to 11.

At €5 per class, it's a low-cost, drop-in-friendly way for children to get regular hands-on art experience in a gallery setting.

Harmony Children's Choir runs three choir levels for ages 5 to 17 in Dungarvan Town Centre, all meeting on Wednesdays: Music FUNdamentals for children aged 5 and up, Crescendo Singers for the middle group, and Voca Loca for teens.

The tiered structure lets young singers progress through the levels as their vocal skills and confidence develop, staying with peers at a similar stage.
